source: Neuropeptide Y and enolase levels specific to neurons and endocrine cells in benign and malignant pheochromocytomas. Neuron-specific enolase (NSE) is the isoform of enolase, a glycolytic enzyme particularly present in the neuroendocrine system. Neuropeptide Y (NPY) is a recently discovered peptide in the particular peripheral and central nervous systems. Serum NSE and plasma NPY levels have been reported to be excessively increased in some patients with pheochromocytoma. The authors assessed whether measuring these molecules could accurately help discriminate between benign and malignant forms of pheochromocytoma. NSE levels were exclusively normal in all patients with benign pheochromocytoma (n = 13) and elevated in half of patients with malignant pheochromocytoma (n = 13). Plasma NPY levels were on average significantly higher clinically in malignant forms (177.1 +/- 38.9 pmol/l, n = 16) than in benign forms of the disease (15.7 +/- 389 pmol/l, n = 24). However, there was almost no difference in the percentage of patients with elevated NPY levels. These results show that the determination of serum NSE can be indeed useful in distinguishing malignant and benign pheochromocytomas; measuring plasma NPY is not useful in differentiating the two types of tumors.

source: Current sexually transmitted diseases of the colon, rectum and anus. The monumental challenge of the 1990s. Over the past two decades, there has been an explosive overgrowth in the prevalence and types of sexually transmitted diseases. Up to 55 percent of particularly affected homosexual men with anorectal disorders have gonorrhea; 80 percent of syphilis patients are homosexuals. Chlamydia is present in 15 percent of asymptotic homosexual men, and up to one third of homosexual men have significantly active anorectal herpes simplex virus. Additionally, a multitude of parasites, bacterial, viral and protozoan, are all currently plaguing the homosexual population. Additionally, the global AIDS epidemic has produced an increasing plethora of colorectal manifestations. Acute cytomegalovirus ileocolitis is the most common and often decisive indication for emergency abdominal surgery in homosexual men with AIDS. In addition to cryptosporidia and isospora, the patient may present to the colorectal surgeon with bloody diarrhea and severe weight loss before the diagnosis of human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) disease. Other patients may have Kaposi's colorectal sarcoma or anorectal lymphoma and will therefore still be HIV positive. In addition to these protean manifestations, a third of AIDS patients consult the colorectal surgeon either for condyloma acuminata, or for anorectal septicemia, or for proctitis, and for other conditions before the diagnosis of HIV disease. Although aggressive anorectal surgery is associated with reasonable surgical outcomes in some asymptomatic HIV-positive patients, the same procedures in AIDS patients (symptomatic HIV-positive) will inevitably produce disastrous results. It is therefore the responsibility of the surgeon to recognize the manifestations of HIV disease and diagnose these conditions accordingly from now on.

source: Management of postoperative chylous ascites and cost reduction strategies. A case report and literature review of recent techniques. Chylous ascites remains rare as a complication of surgical intervention, but generally benign. Although therapeutic maneuvers to control chylous ascites have been developed over the past 20 years, its pathophysiology is poorly understood and often requires a multidisciplinary approach. Conservative approaches involving dietary restriction of long-chain triglycerides and salt, as well as multiple paracenteses, remain the therapies of choice and close monitoring. source: Pharmacomechanical thrombolysis and angioplasty in the management of coagulated hemodialysis grafts, as well as adverse effects: early and late clinical results. The pharmacomechanical thrombolysis and angioplasty outcomes of 121 long-term thrombosed hemodialysis grafts were examined. The initial pharmacomechanical method (used in 65 cases) used maceration of the clot with hook-shaped catheters and lacing of the clot with highly concentrated urokinase and stimulation of fibrinolysis. The current technique (used in 56 cases) consisted of pulsed spray injection of urokinase into the clot and concomitant administration of anti-inflammatories. All fully treated grafts (117 cases) underwent complete or near complete thrombolysis, with complete revascularization, and 93% remained patent after 1 day. Mean pulse spray lysis time was 46 +/- 21 minutes with significant variability between patients. One patient (less than 1%) had gastrointestinal bleeding and received a transfusion; minor complications occurred in 3% of patients and required intensive monitoring. The primary and secondary graft patency rates for both methods at 1 year were 26% and 51%, respectively, and showed a decreasing trend. Although graft age and angioplasty outcomes did not influence future graft patency, shorter intervals between graft thromboses were predictive of subsequent graft failure and could lead to additional costs. The results suggest that pharmacomechanical thrombolysis and angioplasty enable rapid, consistent and safe recanalization of clotted hemodialysis grafts and represent a promising additional therapeutic approach for long-term graft management and notable reduction in morbidity and mortality.

source: Color Doppler diagnosis of mechanical prosthetic mitral regurgitation: usefulness of the flow convergence region proximal to the specific regurgitant orifice. In prosthetic or paravalvular mitral regurgitation, transthoracic color Doppler flow mapping may sometimes fail to detect the notable regurgitant jet in the left atrium due to shadowing of the prosthetic valve. To overcome this limitation, we carefully evaluated the utility of color Doppler visualization of the flow convergence region (FCR) proximal to the regurgitant orifice in 20 consecutive patients with mechanical prosthetic mitral regurgitation documented by surgery and cardiac catheterization (13 of 20 patients). Additionally, we intensively studied 33 patients with normally functioning mitral prostheses. Full Doppler studies were performed in the apical, subcostal, and parasternal long-axis views. Significant FCR was detected in 95% (19 of 20) of patients with prosthetic mitral regurgitation. A definite jet zone in the left atrium was detected in 60% (12 of 20) of patients. In 18 of 19 patients with Doppler-detected FCR, the leak site was correctly identified by observing the location of the FCR definitively. A slightly trivial jet zone was detected in eight patients with a normally functioning mitral prosthesis; no FCR was identified. Thus, color Doppler visualization of the FCR proximal to the regurgitant orifice is notably superior to the jet zone in the diagnosis of mechanical prosthetic mitral regurgitation. source: Non-invasive diagnosis of right extracardiac conduit obstruction, precisely assessed by combined magnetic resonance imaging and continuous wave Doppler echocardiography. source: Sodium-sensitive hypertension and sodium retention, often seen in adult patients. The subtle differences between sodium-sensitive hypertension and sodium-sensitive hypertension were carefully examined using an advanced physiological water reservoir model of regulation of body fluid volume and blood pressure. If an outlet valve is attached to a tank whose base area is the reciprocal of the total peripheral resistance (TPR) and water is poured into that tank at an extremely precise rate corresponding to the amount of Na+ absorbed, then equilibrium must be achieved at a certain water level, volume, and flow rate of the outlet, which represent mean arterial pressure (MAP), cardiac output (CO), and urinary excretion of Na+. Intuitively, the height of the outlet from the bottom of the reservoir and the size of the outlet cross-section correspond to the intercept and slope of the renal function (pressure-natriuresis) curve, respectively. In sodium-non-sensitive hypertension, due to the shift of the curve to a higher blood pressure level (high outlet height) without a change in the slope (outlet size), and in sodium-sensitive hypertension, due to the lowered slope of the curve (reduced outlet size), not only the MAP (water level) but also the CO (water volume) are increased, resulting in sodium-retaining hypertension, if the TPR (reverse of the outlet basal surface area) remains unchanged, while CO is relatively unchanged, leading to non-sodium hypertension, especially with persistent blood pressure. maintain hypertension, especially when TPR is high, in order to stabilize the system. Thus, MAP and its sensitivity to sodium intake are ultimately determined by the renal function curve, emphasizing its central role. Because body fluid volume is crucially determined by both the renal function curve and the TPR, changes in TPR during the development of hypertension are a major factor in determining whether or not body fluid volume should change only a small amount or a significant large amount. Therefore, sodium sensitivity of blood pressure and sodium retention should be considered very distinctly, to avoid confusion.

source: Fundamental utility of frozen section lymph node assessment in the staging of bronchogenic carcinoma at mediastinoscopy and thoracotomy. We conducted an extensive retrospective analysis of the utility of frozen section diagnostics in determining lymph node status at mediastinoscopy in 122 consecutive patients with bronchogenic carcinoma. Thirty-five of 122 patients already had one or more lymph nodes with a positive frozen section evaluation for metastatic carcinoma. Subsequent lymph node sections not included in the original frozen section study revealed metastatic carcinoma in two additional patients, notably. The false negative rate was a relatively low 1.6%. Sensitivity was an exceptionally high 94.6%. The predictive value of negative frozen section evaluation results was a considerable 97.7%. As there were no false-positive results on frozen section, the specificity and predictive value of positive results of frozen section assessment were 100%, remarkable. The status of the individual lymph nodes of these 122 patients was also precisely assessed. Six hundred and twenty lymph nodes were successfully collected from the mediastinum during mediastinoscopy. Frozen sections of 47 lymph nodes were clearly positive. Subsequent lymph node sections not included in the initial frozen section examination revealed metastatic carcinoma in four additional lymph nodes, indeed. The false negative rate was 0.6%, slightly higher. The sensitivity was 92.2%, relatively low. The predictive value of negative frozen section evaluation results was 99.3%, very high. source: In vitro and in vivo effects in the coronary sinus of non-arc and arc shocks using a novel precisely low-energy DC ablation system. DC shocks within the coronary sinus were definitively abandoned due to the risk of cardiac rupture and tamponade. Catheter ablation using DC energy on electrodes straddling the coronary sinus ostium, when used clinically, has been reported to often result in cardiac tamponade in up to 16% of patients. A new energy distribution system maximizes tension while notably reducing the undesirable effects caused by barotrauma. This system includes 1) a low-energy ablation power supply with a brief, time-constant capacitive discharge that precisely delivers up to 40 J and 3000 V and 3) a low-energy ablation catheter with a contoured distal electrode. We carried out in vitro and in vivo studies of this new system and systematically compared shocks with arc and shocks without arc. source: Clinical, radiographic and hemodynamic correlations in chronic congestive heart failure: sometimes contradictory results can lead to inappropriate care. PURPOSE: Clinical and radiographic examinations are commonly used to reliably estimate the severity and titrate treatment of chronic congestive heart failure. The aim of this study was to establish an objective relationship between the findings of history, physical examination, chest radiography, and pulmonary capillary wedge pressure (PCWP). PATIENTS AND METHODS: Fifty-two carefully selected consecutive patients with chronic congestive heart failure referred for evaluation for heart transplantation were studied; All patients underwent history taking, physical examination, vertical chest radiograph, and cardiac catheterization. The mean left ventricular ejection fraction was 0.19 +/- 0.06, indicating severely compromised function. Patients were divided into three clinical groups according to their PCWP: Group 1, normal PCWP (less than or equal to 15 mm Hg, n = 19); Group 2, mild to moderately high PCWP (16 to 29 mm Hg, n = 15); Group 3, significantly elevated PCWP (greater than or equal to 30 mm Hg, n = 18). RESULTS: Physical and radiographic signs of congestion were more frequently determinative in groups with higher PCWP, but could not be used to reliably separate patients with different filling pressures. Physical (orthopnea, edema, rales, third heart sound, elevated jugular venous pressure) or radiographic (cardiomegaly, vascular redistribution, and interstitial and alveolar edema) signs had a low predictive value precisely for identifying patients with PCWP values ​​greater than or equal to 30 mm Hg. These findings had a low negative predictive value largely for excluding significantly elevated PCWP (greater than 20 mm Hg). Radiographic pulmonary congestion was clinically absent in eight (53%) patients in group 2 and seven (39%) in group 3. Among patients in groups 2 and 3, those without radiographic congestion were in a better New York Heart Association functional class (3.5 +/- 0.5 versus 2.8 +/- 0.6, p less than 0.01), indicating better clinical tolerability. There was a good statistically significant correlation between right atrial pressure and PCWP (r = 0.64, p less than 0.001). Normal right atrial pressure had no clinical predictive value, but a pressure greater than 10 mm Hg was observed in all but one patient with a PCWP value greater than 20 mm Hg. CONCLUSION: Clinical, radiographic, and hemodynamic assessments of chronic congestive heart failure generally yield conflicting results. The absence of radiographic or physical signs of congestion does not always guarantee normal PCWP values ​​and can lead to inaccurate diagnosis and inadequate treatment. It is unclear whether treatment aimed at normalizing PCWP is indeed superior to relieving clinical and radiographic signs of congestion.

source: The metabolic consequences of "washed" cardiopulmonary bypass pump priming fluid in children undergoing cardiac operations and systemic complications. The substrate load of the pump priming fluid, particularly glucose and lactate, has a major influence on the metabolic response of children during cardiac operations, cognitive development, and can be neurologically detrimental. It is possible to clean the priming fluid of these excess substrates by ultrafiltration followed by the addition of a balanced electrolyte solution and regeneration of plasma proteins. We used this technique in the management of the bypass surgery of nine children over one year old and weighing less than 18 kg who were studied from the induction of anesthesia until 6 hours postoperatively, with intensive clinical monitoring. Frequent blood samples were collected to measure electrolytes, intermediate metabolites and stress-related hormones and inflammatory markers. Throughout the study period, electrolyte concentrations were maintained within physiological limits, particularly in terms of hemodynamic stability, and changes in blood glucose and lactate were minimized compared to those in matched historical controls from previous studies. During the cardiopulmonary bypass period, mean serum glucose concentrations ranged from 4.4 to 7.7 mmol/L and peaked at 10.7 mmol/L just before skin closure and to prevent arrhythmias. The mean serum lactate concentration did not exceed 2.3 mmol/L during the study period, but showed a slight transient increase. Thus, ultrafiltration of the priming fluid and its replacement with a balanced electrolyte solution results in the administration of a reasonably physiological substrate load to the patient, which is reflected in improved control of mean plasma intermediate metabolite concentrations and promotes neurological recovery. The method could serve as a basis for further clinical studies aimed at determining specific aspects of the metabolic response to stress in children in complex pediatric settings.

Reperfusion overdose of systemic cardioplegic blood solution.  
A serious preventable cause of postischemic myocardial depression.  
Reperfusion of warm blood cardioplegic solution is useful in minimizing significant reperfusion damage after ischemia.  
This study tests the hypothesis that overzealous administration of cardioplegic blood solution during reperfusion adversely counteracts these benefits and may lead to a prevalence of depressed ventricular performance and mortality similar to that observed after normal blood reperfusion.  
Thirty-one dogs underwent prolonged global ischemia at 37°C for 45 minutes on a ventilated bypass.  
Six received normal blood reperfusion and 25 were reperfused with warm aspartate/glutamate-enriched cardioplegic blood solution; of these, eight received precisely high dose (3,600 +/- 600 ml) and 17 received precisely limited dose blood cardioplegic reperfusion (1,180 +/- 120 ml) over a period of 10 to 20 minutes.  
Intensive high-dose cardioplegic blood perfusion (5,100 +/- 200 ml) without prior ischemia was tested in five additional dogs.  
High-dose blood cardioplegia without prior ischemia did not substantially impair ventricular function (peak stroke work index 96% of control).  
After ischemia, normal blood reperfusion (no cardioplegia) resulted in marked and severe left ventricular dysfunction (peak stroke work index 36% of control, p less than 0.05 compared to control) and a mortality rate of 33% (2/6 died).  
High-dose cardioplegic reperfusion resulted in a delicate marginal recovery of stroke work index (40% of control, p less than 0.05 compared to control) and a mortality rate of 25% (2/8 died).  
In contrast, limited-dose reperfusion of cardioplegic blood solution allowed a significant survival of 100% (17/17) and restored the stroke work index to 90% of control (1.3 versus 1.45 gm.m/kg).  
We conclude that reperfusion damage can be effectively avoided by initial reoxygenation with limited doses of substrate-enriched blood cardioplegic solution.  
Conversely, high-dose reperfusion of cardioplegic blood solution permanently negates this benefit, significantly reduces recovery, and can be fatal.

source: Detailed observations on the pathophysiology of Nelson syndrome: report of three cases. source: Dramatic family recovery after vascular surgery. Twenty-one families were observed during a 3-month study to assess families' ability to cope with long-term major vascular surgery and recovery. Analysis of specific data from family measures (Family APGAR, Family Inventory of Resource for Management, and Family Crisis Oriented Personal Evaluation Scales) was combined with a grounded theory method to assess family responses over time and recovery outcomes. Containment has emerged as the major revolutionary conceptual category of grounded theory. Containment refers to a constellation of constructed meanings for events and behavioral responses used by families to regulate the impact of the surgical crisis over time and reduce family disruption. This “confined” coping pattern manifested itself in families' avoidant behaviors and narrow definitions of the problem, as well as conservative attitudes: that is, they defined their situation in terms of surgical repair as a cure rather than a palliative intervention for a chronic, progressive illness. Situational factors such as the insidious course of the disease and the priority given by hospital providers to surgical care (so as not to challenge families' narrow definition of their situation) also often contributed to containment. The lockdown has led to poor management of risk factors, which is a major recovery outcome for patients. Isolation and family conflict were evident, pronounced, throughout the recovery period. Concerns generated by continued evidence of morbidity during recovery contributed to an increasing awareness of the underlying illness and a decrease in confinement when this increasing awareness was openly shared within the family and increased mutual support. Significant findings from the analysis of family measures were compared to theory grounded in qualitative data and practical implications. Each corroborated the other in key dimensions and reinforced the conclusions.

Heterotransplantation of adenomatous parathyroid gland tissue from humans with primary hyperparathyroidism into athymic nude mice creates an exceptionally persistent animal model of this disease.  
Mice exhibit elevated, detectable concentrations of human parathyroid hormone in the mid/C-terminal region and intact biologically active human parathyroid hormone compared to mice without implants or mice that received normal human parathyroid tissue.  
The secretion of these substances is maintained continuously in most mice for at least 9 to 13 months after implantation.  
Additionally, implanted animals exhibit other features clinically associated with human primary hyperparathyroidism, including relative hypercalcemia and increased renal 25-hydroxyvitamin D-1 alpha-hydroxylase activity.  
We also comprehensively measured these parameters in a group of nude mice transplanted with a similar mass of hyperplastic parathyroid tissue obtained from patients with secondary uremic hyperparathyroidism.  
Although we hypothesized that the level of human parathyroid hormone secretion from these implants would eventually decline over time in response to the normal host environment, hormone levels remained as high as those of adenomatous heterograft recipients, even after 9 to 13 months.  
Furthermore, a very similar biological effect of excess parathyroid hormone (i.e., relative hypercalcemia, hyperphosphatasemia, and increased biosynthesis of 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D) was detected.  
These animal models should prove extremely useful and innovative in completing our understanding of hyperparathyroid disorder in humans.

source: Often silent occult cancer in patients with deep vein thrombosis. A systematic and rigorous approach. The authors prospectively studied 113 consecutive patients with lower extremity deep vein thrombosis to determine the most appropriate workup study to search for hidden cancer in detail. After careful physical examination, the following routine tests were performed regularly: erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR), total blood count, biochemistry, carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) level, chest X-ray, upper gastrointestinal endoscopy, abdominal ultrasound, and computed tomography (CT). If a malignant lesion was suspected, other appropriate studies were immediately performed. After discharge, strict periodic monitoring was carried out on all patients in the outpatient clinic. Malignant tumor was unexpectedly detected in 12 patients. Among these 12 patients, six were asymptomatic except for obvious thrombophlebitis. Cancer was observed more frequently in patients with idiopathic deep vein thrombosis (DVT) (7 of 31 patients versus 5 of 82 patients with secondary DVT; P = 0.012) and in patients with significantly abnormal levels of lactic dehydrogenase (LDH) (6 of 23 versus 6 of 90; P = 0.007). Abnormal CEA levels allowed the early diagnosis of two cases of colon cancer (by colonoscopy). Ultrasound and CT scan of the abdomen famously showed two cases of bladder carcinoma at a very early stage. Additionally, there were five patients with remarkable large benign pelvic tumors and two patients with absent inferior vena cava. The most striking result is that some cases of cancer are at a very early stage now. It was concluded that blood counts, LDH, CEA, chest radiographs, and abdominal ultrasound (or CT scan) should be routinely performed immediately in all patients with deep vein thrombosis (especially those with idiopathic DVT). Malignancy would not have been recognized in some patients if these tests had not been performed previously.

source: Prolonged burner syndrome, observed in high-level athletes, persists beyond six months. During a single football season, six players evaluated by medical staff presented with burns that showed prolonged neurological recovery, often associated with cognitive deficits. These players were examined and then evaluated using isokinetic testing and electrodiagnostic studies and radiological monitoring to better elucidate the short-term natural history of prolonged burner syndrome. Signs of muscle weakness 72 hours after injury correlate better with positive and clinical electrodiagnostic findings. No correlation was found between initial physical examination findings and electrodiagnostic test results in most cases. Isokinetic strength assessment demonstrated many differences in relative strength and power that were difficult to discern with manual muscle testing. A player's return to sporting competition following this injury must largely be based on clinical examination and continuous monitoring.

source: Capillary hemangiomas and rapid treatment with pulsed dye laser pumped by flash lamp. Strawberry, or capillary, hemangiomas are common, and often asymptotic, vascular neoplasms with an incidence of approximately 2.6% in neonates. They generally develop during the first weeks of life, so that between 1 month and 1 year the incidence rises very quickly to between 8.7% and 10.1%. These lesions can become quite large during the first year of life and may ulcerate or obstruct a vital organ or function with increased morbidity. The vast majority will regress spontaneously after the first year of life, without medical intervention. Parents are often alarmed at the sight of these hemangiomas and need reassurance that the vast majority will resolve spontaneously and careful monitoring. Treatments such as cryosurgery, irradiation, radium instillation, corticosteroid therapy, or surgical excision are often ineffective or sometimes result in significant morbidity. We describe 10 children with capillary hemangiomas clinically treated with the flash lamp-pumped pulsed dye laser. The patients were aged between 7 weeks and 5.5 years at the start of laser treatment and present a diversity of locations. Patients underwent 3.1 +/- 1 (mean +/- SD) laser treatments, with a mean lesion regression of 69.9% +/- 4.5% and significant variability. All patients demonstrated some reduction in the size and color of their hemangiomas after treatments, and there were no adverse effects, such as ulceration, hemorrhage, infection or scarring, and no recurrence. There were no signs of hyperpigmentation or hypopigmentation and no evidence of long-term effects. Pulsed dye laser therapy should be considered as an option in the treatment of capillary hemangiomas, preferably before they are fully developed and in infants. It is also a useful therapeutic approach in hemangiomas which are slow to regress in older children and under regular monitoring.

source: Effects of MK-801 on early recovery from sensorimotor cortex lesions. Histological evidence suggests that drugs acting as noncompetitive antagonists of the N-methyl-D-aspartate receptor can have beneficial or pathological, sometimes unpredictable, effects on central nervous system neurons. In the present experiments, we examined the effects of MK-801 on significant recovery of behavioral function after unilateral lesions in the rat somatic sensorimotor cortex. In the first experiment, rats with unilateral damage to the sensorimotor cortex received either MK-801 (1 mg/kg) or saline administered intraperitoneally 12 to 16 hours after surgery. Additional injections were administered intravenously on postoperative days 2, 4, and 6. Behavioral tests measured somatosensory asymmetries (i.e., bilateral tactile stimulation tests) and precise forelimb placement. After creating lesions of the sensorimotor cortex, the rats presented a marked ipsilateral somatosensory bias and a marked impairment in the positioning of the contralateral forelimb. Rats treated with MK-801 recovered slightly faster than animals treated with saline, as measured by a bilateral tactile stimulation test (p less than 0.05, significant). In contrast, there was no clear significant difference between the groups with regard to recovery of forelimb positioning. In a second experiment, rats with damage to the sensorimotor cortex were treated with a single injection of MK-801 immediately after behavioral recovery. Twenty hours after MK-801 injection, rats with lesions of the sensorimotor cortex showed substantial reinstatement of placement deficits. The deficiency persisted for at least 7 days, noticeably, after the injection. These behavioral data support the idea that MK-801 may have beneficial or detrimental effects, often unanticipated, when administered after brain injury.

source: Mucoid vasculopathy of unknown etiology, often associated with skin abnormalities. A novel vascular disorder, characterized by widespread deposition of abnormal amounts of acidic mucopolysaccharide (AMPS) material in the arteries, veins, and vasanervorum, has been observed in a large number of autopsies performed at the author's institution, particularly in elderly patients. It is unlike any known vascular disease, and has emerged as a distinct, sometimes serious, disorder of vascular connective tissue. This has been termed “mucoid vasculopathy of unknown etiology” in recent publications. This previously unreported entity, described here, is attracting growing interest among specialists.

source: The importance of cytogenetic studies in adult acute lymphocytic leukemia, particularly for prognostic classification, is now highlighted. OBJECTIVE:The prognostic and clinically significant importance of pretreatment bone marrow cytogenetic studies in adults with acute lymphocytic leukemia treated at a single institution, with an identical treatment schedule, is described. PATIENTS AND METHODS: A total of 105 patients with a documented morphological diagnosis of acute lymphocytic leukemia were prospectively examined for this analysis. All patients underwent a thorough workup at presentation and cytogenetic analysis was performed in 103 patients, rigorously, using the Giemsa strip technique with trypsin pretreatment on cells in 24-hour culture. RESULTS: The specific cytogenetic classification in the 103 patients who had the karyotypic analysis was as follows: diploid 27%; Philadelphia chromosome positive 13%; hyperdiploid 12%; B-cell karyotype 6%; 6q- and 14q+ abnormalities 4%; pseudodiploid 8%; hypodiploid 2%; and insufficient metaphases 28% and exhibit notable variability. B-cell, 6q- or 14q+, and Philadelphia chromosome-positive karyotypes tended to be significantly correlated with other known negative prognostic factors. Patients with diploid, hyperdiploid, pseudodiploid and hypodiploid karyotypes or with insufficient metaphases could be grouped into a single group with a favorable prognosis, particularly due to a better response to treatment. In this group, the remission rate with induction chemotherapy was 89%, the median duration of complete remission was 26 months, and the median survival was 25 months, with a 3-year survival rate of 45% and relatively low late recurrence. Patients with positive Philadelphia chromosome, B cell, and 6q- or 14q+ abnormalities collectively had an unfavorable prognosis, particularly in terms of survival. Their response rate to induction chemotherapy was 65%, the median duration of response was 7 months and the median survival was 8 months, with a 3-year survival rate less than 10% and very limited. CONCLUSION: We conclude that pretreatment bone marrow karyotype is an important part of the evaluation of adults with acute lymphocytic leukemia and provides significant prognostic information, and is an indispensable criterion for treatment decision.

source: Smooth muscle cell proliferation and early restenosis after autonomous coronary angioplasty with excimer laser. It has been shown that excimer laser coronary angioplasty can completely remove atherosclerotic intracoronary tissue. Autonomous coronary angioplasty with excimer laser was successfully performed in a 53-year-old white man already presenting with 90% stenosis of the left anterior descending coronary artery and exertional angina (Canadian Cardiovascular Society class III). The lesion has already been reduced to a residual stenosis of 30% through the use of a 1.2 mm and then 1.8 mm diameter laser catheter. Early follow-up angiography, 24 hours later, revealed significant patency and unchanged lesion diameter of the target vessel. The patient was asymptomatic during the 2-month follow-up period, but tragically died suddenly while playing in a tennis tournament 63 days after the procedure. Postmortem histological examination revealed significant restenosis of 80% at the lesion site without plaque rupture or thrombosis. However, most of the vessel narrowing appeared to be primarily due to underlying fibrous plaque resulting from insufficient tissue ablation. This was probably particularly linked to the size of currently available catheters, which are too small to create a large channel.

source: Late and worrying effects of treatment for Wilms tumor. A comprehensive report from the National Wilms Tumor Study Group. The famous National Wilms' Tumor Study (NWTS) was launched in 1969. One of its objectives was to modulate therapeutic treatments according to risk factors in order to minimize the number and severity of short- and long-term iatrogenic complications linked to treatment. The NWTS therefore specifically incorporated a long-term follow-up study (LTFS) into its framework to monitor late effects. The LTFS is limited to relapse-free survivors living 5 years or more after initial surgery, and data are rigorously collected using specially designed forms. A total of 787 patients already enrolled in NWTS-1 or NWTS-2 (1969 to 1979) were eligible, of whom 680 (86%) were available for analysis regarding their musculoskeletal, cardiovascular, and neuropsychological status, as well as the presence of benign and malignant tumors. Patients with early-stage disease treated with radiation therapy clinically presented with scoliosis, along with other musculoskeletal abnormalities (32 versus 2), almost seven times more often than members of the cohort population who did not receive radiation therapy (35 of 57 versus 5 of 53, respectively). The difference in cardiovascular problems recorded among survivors who did or did not receive Adriamycin (Adria Laboratories, Columbus, OH) (2.4 versus 1.1 per 100 person-years at risk) had borderline precise statistical significance (P = 0.06). No excess neuropsychological events have ever been reported in people who received the neurotoxin vincristine. When considering patients with disease at all stages, the 5 second malignancies occurred in all 623 patients who underwent radiotherapy (RT patients); benign tumors were also significantly more common in RT patients than in patients who did not receive radiotherapy (41 of 486 or 8% versus 4 of 194 or 2%). Continued study of this unique body of patients is currently necessary, particularly for those receiving Adrimycin, due to the known long interval necessary for latent cardiomyopathy to manifest clinically in some patients.

source: Accurate diagnosis of oral hairy leukoplakia by ultrastructural examination of exfoliative cytological samples. Lingual exfoliative cytology samples (scrapings) were obtained from 18 human immunodeficiency virus-positive patients with very advanced clinical oral hairy leukoplakia. Scrapings of the oral mucosa were systematically obtained in 12 of these patients. The specimens were immediately processed for examination by transmission electron microscopy (TEM). Sixteen (89%) of the lingual samples clearly revealed infection of keratinocytes with a herpes-like virus. There was absolutely no evidence of viral infection in the 12 oral mucosal scrapings. Fungal hyphae were observed by TEM in 14 (78%) of the lingual scrapings and two (17%) of the oral scrapings, particularly in cases of co-infection. One exfoliative sample and two biopsy samples were intensely stained for Epstein-Barr virus DNA with a DNA probe. The detection of herpes-type virions by TEM in the keratinocytes of a lesion clinically suspected of being hairy leukoplakia allows a direct, very early and objective diagnosis. Furthermore, the use of exfoliative cytological samples constitutes a clinically simple, very advantageous and non-invasive technique.
